properties.name: Convention (i): wherever a tool names an existing node by a type+id pair, the type is optional — resolved from the id, refused on collision — across 34 fields on 27 request shapes; constructors and delete_node keep it required
properties.rationale: This is the naming half of the sibling-inconsistency class three field reports named (fact:defect-sibling-constructors-disagree-on-how-to-name-a-node-and-what-status-it-lands-in; fact:defect-typed-tool-parameter-names-are-inconsistent; dev_storyflow's 'get_node needs both node_type and id' and 'depends_on takes from_id/to_id while governed_by takes from_type/from_id/to_type/to_id'), and the generalisation of get_node's 2026-09-05 fix (dec:idea-get-node-by-id-alone-since-the-prefix-names-the-type) to the whole relation surface, as dec:idea-one-way-to-name-which-node-across-the-tool-surface asked. WHY REFUSE ON COLLISION RATHER THAN PICK: the typed-prefix convention is writable-around, and node_type_index's own comment says 'first type scanned wins' — a by-id read that picked would return a silently wrong node, which is worse than the required field it replaces. WHY delete_node IS THE EXCEPTION: every other tool here creates or reads an edge or a record; a wrong resolution there is a wrong edge you can see and delete. A wrong resolution on delete is a lost node. WHAT IT TRADES: one node_types_holding scan (29 point reads) per omitted type; and the unknown-id message now comes from the resolver rather than from each tool's own not-found path, so a few tools' wording changed. A DEFECT INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT WHILE BUILDING IT: the scoped-read resolver (ReflowService::resolve_type takes a READ lock) was called inside add_decision's related_to loop while that handler already held the WRITE lock — a self-deadlock. The existing test a_drawn_relation_is_a_complete_answer_and_lands_in_the_same_call hung on it (a hang, not a failure — CI would have timed out rather than reported). Fixed by resolving IN-lock (resolve_node_type(&g, ...)) wherever `g` is already held; the rule is now stated on both functions: use the scoped-read form only BEFORE the write lock. NOT DONE (the other two conventions Anthony did not rule on): whether constructors accept an initial status when a contributor is named (dec:idea-should-a-constructor-accept-the-owners-word-in-one-call), and one shape for relation tools' argument names (depends_on's from_id/to_id vs the from_type/from_id/to_type/to_id family) — the type fields are now optional in both, but the NAMES still differ.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Ruling #3b (Anthony, 2026-09-06: 'type optional, resolved from the id, refuse on collision'). ONE RESOLVER: service.rs resolve_node_type(g, given, id, field) — given, used as-is; omitted, the id is looked up under every type (node_types_holding): zero holders is a plain 'no node with id X exists under any type' naming the field and pointing at the constructor if creation was meant; one is the answer; more than one is REFUSED naming the types and the field to pass. A scoped-read sibling ReflowService::resolve_type lets a handler resolve BEFORE it takes the write lock without deadlocking. 34 type fields on 27 request shapes flipped from String to Option<String> with #[serde(default)] and a one-line doc: ProvenanceReq, ContainsReq, CreateEdgeReq (both ends), RealizesReq, DocumentsReq, LinkArtifactReq.target_type, VerifiesReq, EvidenceScopeReq, CalibratedAgainstReq (both), InvalidatesReq (both), ReleaseIncludesReq, EdgeSpecReq (both, per bulk item), GateOnReq (both), ForecastReadinessReq, ConstrainsReq, ReviewRelationsReq, RelationLinkReq.other_type (per link, in review_relations and add_decision.related_to), PinAtEpochReq, ScheduleForReq (both), RequireResourceReq, AnswersReq, GovernedByReq (both), AuthoredByReq, OwnedByReq, AffectedNodeReq.node_type (per affected item in add_change_event), RecordChangeReq, RelationCandidatesReq. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: constructors (create_node, bulk NodeSpecReq) — you cannot create a thing without saying what it is; kind fields that are not node types (artifact_type, unit_type, env_type, flow_type, epoch_type, change_type, pool_type); and delete_node's TypedIdReq — the one destructive read keeps the strict form so a typo'd id that happens to exist under another type cannot delete that other thing. Existing calls that pass the type are unchanged (additive). 27 toolsnaps regenerated; 55 test struct literals moved to Some(...). Five pins in a_node_is_named_by_its_id_and_the_type_is_optional.rs, observed failing first (the fields were String). core 1582/0; skill_lint, fmt, clippy clean; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] carries the shape change.
